block.title: The abyss ark diving free, silhouette retreating into the dark
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; ending scene painted at hi-resolution, dread preserved, ultra-detailed large-format art with pixel-texture accents. The one that got away, and the one who watched it go: in the far middle-right of the frame, a colossal whale-bodied fortress-ark is diving — thirteen segments of armored hull-plate arcing downward into a black ocean trench, the great tail fluke still above the surface mid-stroke, each plate-seam and porthole-row of the beast lit in its own faint ring of cold bioluminescent teal, a lantern-procession of the ship's own silhouette marking its descent into the deep. The water it displaces climbs the frame in slow carved walls and collapsing shelves of foam, all back-lit by the last light; the sky it leaves is a bruised pre-dawn of deep navy and ash-rose, the surface unbroken everywhere except along the diving creature's fading wake-line. In the bottom-left foreground, tiny and level on the swells, a single steel-blue dart fighter hangs with one engine idling, canopy glinting a thin cyan edge, visibly not pursuing — the two lights of the ark winking out one segment at a time as the last honest view of the IRON TIDE slips beneath and away. The composition gives the dark half its victory: more than a third of the frame is the black water the ark is entering, and it closes over the ship with quiet relish. Palette of ash-navy dawn, teal biolume accents, foam greys, lifted deep-navy shadows, never pure black. No text, no letters, no UI.

block.notes: Biolume porthole teal ~#6ad8e0 dimming to #16485a as it descends; ark plate silhouette echoes the AA-09 bestiary. This is a bad-ending key art: no fire, no loss, just scale refusing to die — resist any model urge to add explosions or a chase. Foreground fighter is one engine idling, low left, facing the ark; his stillness is the meaning.
